Image2 is the confirmed MAIN STYLE: clean bright rounded Daoist chibi hand-painted materials, delicate warm shading, crisp finished edges. Image3 is the front-action scale and weapon construction reference, not this new view: preserve its chibi head/body proportions, outfit details, gear scale and consistent two-hand grip, then draw the correct new view and specified leg phase. Image4 fixes the same-direction camera, silhouette size, costume back construction and spear orientation; genuinely redraw the requested different leg phase, do not reproduce its pose. Facing NORTHEAST diagonally away toward screen upper-right, exact 45-degree right-rear three-quarter view. Show the back and her right side, not a front or front-three-quarter face. Anatomical LEFT leg is the far leg projecting upper-left of the near right hip; anatomical RIGHT leg is near. Forward foot moves along screen UPPER-RIGHT, rear foot is screen LOWER-LEFT. Never swap which knee belongs to which hip. Keep fixed slightly elevated game camera, no camera roll, same rounded short-limb proportion as Image3. Center grounded body around x512, contact-root around y942 on a 1024 canvas (scale fractions if native resolution differs). Entire head, twin tails, red ribbons, wide sleeves, spear tip, spear butt and both boots inside canvas with margin; match Image3 relative subject scale. Her anatomical LEFT hand always grips higher on the shaft nearer the blade at chest level; anatomical RIGHT hand grips lower near waist. Rear-view arms and shaft can naturally occlude behind the torso; do not put a second weapon on her back. WALK PHASE 09 of 16 (one complete alternating left-right cycle, 30ms per frame): Anatomical RIGHT boot is forward in the walking direction, heel-first initial ground contact; anatomical LEFT leg trails back with toe still touching ground and heel raised. Brief double support, right leading. This is the opposite leading leg to phase01, no mirror or copy. Gentle short-step grounded walk with minimal vertical bob; stable upright torso. Hair, skirt, ribbons and tassels react subtly, not wildly. At least one foot supports the ground in every walk. Knees and feet stay on two distinct anatomical tracks, no crossed legs, twisted feet, wide splits, jumping, running, attack, high-knee portrait pose, or large sole facing viewer. Highest visual finish, clean alpha edges without purple/magenta fringe. Preserve Image4 right-rear camera and straight spear upper-left to lower-right. Exchange the leading leg relative to Image4: anatomical RIGHT NEAR leg now forward toward screen UPPER-RIGHT with heel just grounded; anatomical LEFT FAR leg trails toward screen LOWER-LEFT with toe still grounded and heel raised. Clearly trace near right hip knee boot forward. Do not repeat near-right trailing pose of Image4. Short double support, not airborne.
